text:
maria: Heads-up — embeddings/rerank lane started returning 429s in us-east-1 ~15:20. Queue depth spiked to ~6k, GPUs at 98% and KV cache thrash. Notable latency bump for low-QPS customers too.
ajay: saw it, alerted on-call. Looks like a single partner traffic burst hitting high-concurrency rerank workloads.
kai: can you paste the runbook metrics? I want to see per-lane admission and current lane split.
maria: pasted logs excerpt and a quick query below. queue_length_by_lane: rerank=6200, embed=900, rerank_gpu_util=98%.
```
# prometheus-ish query
sum(queue_depth) by (lane)
http_requests_total{route="/v1/rerank"}
```
ajay: the traffic pattern is 20s spikes of 250 qps per connection — continuous for ~10m windows. Our default admission (global 2k concurrency) got overwhelmed because rerank wasn't limited per-customer.
sam: hmm — current per-customer rate limit only applies to host-level qps, not to lane concurrency. We need token-bucket at lane-level + per-customer cap.
elaine: for short term can we throttle that partner to reduce 429 cascades? We should also avoid routing other customers into the same rerank pool.
kai: suggestion: create a soft admission control gate for rerank lane that enforces: min(allocated_capacity, global_limit_per_lane) and add a per-customer cap of 100 concurrent requests. If exceeded, respond with 429 + Retry-After or 202 queued?
maria: agreed. I'm going to spin up a temporary dedicated rerank pool (smaller instances) and move non-critical rerank traffic there to relieve hot path. That buys time for policy change.
sre-bot: incident created — INC-2026-122: us-east rerank lane saturation. Assigned: ajay, maria.
ajay: can we also adjust admission to prefer cached prefixes: i.e., prioritize requests with KV cache hits to keep tail latency low. We should instrument hit-rate in admission decisions.
elaine: cost note — spinning extra dedicated GPUs for rerank will bump short-term infra spend. Recommend auto-scale up with strict cool-down and set a timebox (2h).
mar ia: typo — maria: will do 2h, then re-evaluate. Also adding a temporary rate-limit rule in the edge LB for that partner: 120 qps, burst 300.
kai: small change for rollout: update routing policy config -> add lane_admission:{"rerank": {"per_customer_concurrency": 100, "priority":"cache_hit"}}. Test in staging first.
sam: I'll take staging test, run k6 load with a synthetic spike, and validate fallback behavior.
ajay: follow-up: we should consider permanent separation of high-cost rerank models into a dedicated capacity lane with committed slots (reserved GPUs) to avoid noisy neighbor issues. Patch notes for product discussion.
elaine: +1, capture cost/benefit for product.
maria: short-term actions: 1) edge rate-limit partner (applied) 2) spin temporary dedicated rerank pool (in progress) 3) implement lane-level token-bucket + per-customer caps (PR queued) 4) instrument KV cache hits in admission path.
sre-bot: update — edge rule applied successfully.
kai: thanks — once PR passes, let's rollout canary to 10% of rerank traffic. If canary stable for 15m, promote.
ajay: leaving notes for oncall: monitor queue_depth, rerank_gpu_util, 429_rate by customer. If 429_rate > 1% for >5m, rollback routing changes and scale up pool.
maria: any objections? :thumbsup: to proceed on the plan.
sam: :thumbsup:
elaine: :thumbsup:
kai: :thumbsup:
